identity.title: Learning dynamics in linear recurrent neural networks

problem.claim: Analyze how linear recurrent neural networks learn tasks with temporal dependencies, including how task temporal structure affects learning.

gap.claim: Existing RNN theory leaves limited understanding of the learning process and the impact of temporal data structure.

contributions.claim: An analytical framework for LRNN learning dynamics that accounts for task dynamics.
Four reported properties concerning singular-value learning order, stability and extrapolation, effective regularization and computation tradeoffs, and recurrence-driven feature learning.
A proof-of-concept application of the framework to LRNNs performing sensory integration tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their work provides a first analytical treatment of the relationship between temporal task dependencies and LRNN learning dynamics, including a novel finite-width LRNN neural tangent kernel derivation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that larger singular values and singular values associated with later temporal positions are learned faster.

The authors report that task dynamics affect solution stability and extrapolation ability, while the loss induces effective small-weight regularization and a recurrent-versus-feedforward computation tradeoff.
The authors report using the framework to explain LRNN behavior on sensory integration tasks as a proof of concept.

narrative_sequence.summary: RNNs are used for temporal tasks and neural-dynamics modeling, but their learning process and sensitivity to temporal data structure remain insufficiently understood.
The paper introduces an analytical LRNN framework that incorporates task dynamics.

The analysis reports four properties linking temporal order and scale to learning, task dynamics to stability and extrapolation, loss geometry to computation allocation, and recurrence to feature learning.
The framework is applied as a proof of concept to sensory integration behavior.
The authors position the analysis as a foundation for understanding emergent dynamic behavior in cognitive models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states a compact set of distinct theoretical properties and connects each to a specific mechanism or consequence, such as temporal precedence, stability, regularization, or feature learning.

lessons.interpretation: A contribution can be made more informative by pairing each formal result with the behavior or design tradeoff it explains.
lessons.application: When presenting theory, organize results as mechanism-to-consequence claims and preserve decisive qualifiers such as scale, temporal position, or finite width.
lessons.exception: This structure is unsuitable when the work does not establish distinct mechanisms or when the abstract cannot support the claimed consequences.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify assumptions, model parameterization, optimization regime, task distributions, or quantitative sensory-integration results.
The reported proof-of-concept explanation is not accompanied by comparison metrics or experimental conditions.
